page: Amazon Web Services m8gb.4xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, this instance features 16 dedicated physical cores running at 2.8 GHz with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory performance, with a Passmark memory score in the top tier and large-block memory read and write bandwidths categorized as strong at 296.88 GB/sec and 138.33 GB/sec respectively. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong at 203.02 GB/sec. General CPU benchmarks, such as Geekbench and stress-ng, fall into the average range. Database operations perform strongly, registering 24236.19 on Passmark, while Redis SET operations average 34.43 million operations per second.

The instance provides a baseline network bandwidth of 33 Gbps. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture delivers a high-density resource profile, offering dedicated physical cores and high memory bandwidth without the premium of traditional architectures. This server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, database operations, web serving, and multi-threaded data decompression tasks. It is less optimal for large language model inference, where text generation speeds for 7B models average 19.51 tokens per second.
